Priya (Acme): Hey team — our March invoice (INV-2026-03-ACME) is showing a $27.03 charge but the dashboard usage for the same period shows $26.76. Can someone explain the gap?
Lina (Billing): Sorry for the trouble, Priya. Can you paste the invoice lines (redacted) and the dashboard snapshot URL?
Priya (Acme): Here are the two interesting invoice lines (redacted):
```
2026-03-01, text-generation, 134,512 tokens, $13.4512
2026-03-02, embeddings, 68,900 tokens, $6.8900
... subtotal rounding adjustments -> $27.03
```
And dashboard shows per-route totals that sum to $26.76 for the same dates. Screenshot: https://example.com/snap/abc123
Ajay (Support): Thanks — two quick hypotheses: 1) per-request rounding vs aggregated rounding when converting token-unit prices to cents, 2) VAT/tax bucketization in EU vs dashboard net amounts. Which currency is invoice in?
Priya (Acme): Invoice is in USD, customer located in CA. No VAT. Dashboard currency is USD as well.
Carlos (Eng): Can you also share a small sample of raw usage events? If the billing pipeline rounds each request to the cent and then sums, that can create a delta vs summing raw token counts then applying pricing.
Priya (Acme): Here's a tiny CSV snippet of three requests we think matter: 
```
ts,route,tokens
2026-03-01T08:12:11Z,generate,5
2026-03-01T08:12:12Z,generate,4
2026-03-01T08:12:13Z,generate,3
```
Ajay (Support): OK — those tiny per-request token counts can produce micro-remainders once we convert to $ per-token and then round to cents per-line. The dashboard shows raw tokens aggregated (no per-request cent rounding). Invoice ledger historically applied per-request rounding at the line-item level for backwards compatibility.
Lina (Billing): Confirming: invoice_line = round(tokens * unit_price, 2) for each request then sum(lines). Dashboard uses sum(tokens) * unit_price then round once. That will create small differences, especially with lots of microcalls.
Priya (Acme): Is there a recommended workaround? Our app bursts many tiny calls and that magnifies the drift.
Carlos (Eng): Short term: we can aggregate at the proxy layer on your side to batch small calls, or we can issue an invoice credit to make you whole while we fix. Long term: we're updating the billing pipeline to align aggregation semantics (apply pricing after summing tokens per invoice line) — will reduce these discrepancies.
Ajay (Support): Repro steps I used to validate locally:
1) Pull raw events for customer for date range.
2) Calculate A = sum(round(tokens_i * price_per_token, 2))
3) Calculate B = round(sum(tokens_i) * price_per_token, 2)
4) Compare A - B -> should match your delta.
Example SQL we ran: 
```
SELECT
  customer_id,
  SUM(ROUND(tokens * 0.0001, 2)) AS per_request_round_sum,
  ROUND(SUM(tokens) * 0.0001, 2) AS aggregate_round_sum,
  SUM(ROUND(tokens * 0.0001, 2)) - ROUND(SUM(tokens) * 0.0001, 2) AS delta_cents
FROM billing.events
WHERE customer_id = 'acme' AND date BETWEEN '2026-03-01' AND '2026-03-31'
GROUP BY customer_id;
```
Lina (Billing): Filed internal ticket WIND-3456 to change ledger aggregation to aggregate-first for new invoices and add a reconciliation flag.
Priya (Acme): Appreciate it. Can you confirm whether the $27.03 will be corrected for this month?
Ajay (Support): We will issue a one-off invoice credit of $0.27 to reconcile this invoice and keep you posted on the pipeline change.
Carlos (Eng): Notes for the fix: - change billing calc to use high-precision decimal (no intermediate cents), - aggregate tokens per invoice_line_key before applying rounding, - add unit tests for large number of micro-requests. Target: patch in next billing cycle (ETA 2 weeks).
Priya (Acme): Thanks. Any chance to get a short note in the invoice description so our finance team sees the credit?
Lina (Billing): Yes — credit will be labeled: "Adjustment: per-request rounding reconciliation (WIND-3456)" and applied to INV-2026-03-ACME.
BillingBot: :white_check_mark: Credit issued (CR-8921) for $0.27 against INV-2026-03-ACME.
Priya (Acme): :pray: thanks everyone. Small thing but important for monthly close.
Carlos (Eng): Also logging a perf note — if you can batch at least 10 tokens per request you will see amortized cost drop and fewer rounding artifacts.
Ajay (Support): Follow-ups: I'll DM Priya the reconciliation CSV and add this thread to the billing postmortem doc.
Lina (Billing): Closing loop here; will update once WIND-3456 is rolled out. :thumbsup:
